key_insight: Introduce an efficient camera-alignment reward feedback mechanism that lets video diffusion models learn stronger, more accurate camera control by assessing alignment without expensive RGB decoding.
problem_solved: Camera-controlled video diffusion models still struggle to follow desired camera trajectories: existing reward-feedback (ReFL) methods lack a camera-aware reward model and computing rewards by decoding latents to RGB is computationally costly and slow.
method: Design a camera-aware reward model that evaluates video↔camera alignment (trained to recognize trajectory, framing, and motion consistency).
Compute reward signals efficiently in latent space (or via a compact camera encoder) to avoid full RGB decoding for every sample.
Integrate the efficient reward into a ReFL loop to fine-tune the video diffusion model, improving its camera-controllability while keeping compute low.
impact: Makes camera-conditioned video generation more reliable and practical by improving alignment accuracy and drastically lowering reward-evaluation cost—accelerating research and deployment of controllable generative video systems.

paper_title: CamPilot: Improving Camera Control in Video Diffusion Model with Efficient Camera Reward Feedback
paper_authors: Wenhang Ge, Guibao Shen, Jiawei Feng, Luozhou Wang, Hao Lu
